# Kaṇḍarījātaka (Ja 341)

**ID:** Ja 341
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kaṇḍarījātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** On Kaṇḍarī

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kaṇḍarījātaka* (Ja 341) is a birth story located in the *Kokilavagga* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1883]. In the canonical and commentary arrangement at this location, the story itself is not presented in full; rather, the text explicitly notes that the detailed narrative (*vitthārakathā*) is set forth in the *Kuṇālajātaka* (Ja 536) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. 

As recorded in the Kuṇālajātaka commentary and discussed in secondary scholarship, the narrative concerns King Kaṇḍarī of Bārāṇasī, his wife Queen Kinnarā, and the king's wise chaplain (*purohita*) Pañcālacanda [Fausböll 1891; Riccardi]. Queen Kinnarā betrays and leaves her husband for a cripple (*pīṭhasappi*), forming one of several misogynous narratives collected in the Kuṇāla birth story [Fausböll 1891; Riccardi]. Discussing the textual history of the story, Heinrich Lüders and Willem Bollée noted that the compound *Kandarikannarānam* was misdivided as *Kandari-kinnarānam*, giving the title *Kandari-jātaka* to what had once been an independent jātaka [Riccardi]. Bollée also observed that the tale circulated widely and reached Nepal, where it was recited by Newar Vajrācāryas [Riccardi].

SuttaCentral lists the *Kuṇālajātaka* (Ja 536) as the parallel to this text [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with this, DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal text reuse between Ja 341 and Ja 536 (4 matches totaling 1,028 characters, with Ja 341 §1.1–4.4 corresponding to Ja 536 §60.1–63.4 with 0.98 similarity), as well as matches with the fifth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (8 matches, 782 characters) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring machine alignments with a Tibetan translation of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtra* (D0555) [DharmaNexus].
